title: Shore Fishing Around Shediac & Cocagne, NB
intro_md:
Cocagne and Shediac sit on the Northumberland Strait coast of Kent and Westmorland Counties, New Brunswick, about 30-45 minutes northeast of Moncton. Cocagne is built around the mouth of the Cocagne River and Cocagne Bay, with the Cocagne Cape Marina and its breakwater a well-known local fishing spot. Shediac — the self-styled "Lobster Capital of the World" — sits on Shediac Bay, a large tidal embayment fed by the Shediac River, Scoudouc River, and Bateman Brook, with Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf and Parlee Beach as its best-known shore access points.

This whole stretch is tidal estuary and open Northumberland Strait coastline, meaning nearly everything in this guide is saltwater/tidal fishing that does not require a provincial licence. Local anglers note that fishing pressure around Moncton itself is heavy, so the Cocagne-Shediac shoreline and the drive further northeast toward Bouctouche and Kouchibouguac tends to fish better than in-town spots.

**Regulations overview**: New Brunswick recreational saltwater fishing is managed by Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO), Gulf Region — the same regional office and rules that apply across the southern Gulf of St. Lawrence (PEI, NS, and NB). No provincial licence is needed for tidal-water species (striped bass, mackerel, flounder, smelt, eel, etc.). A New Brunswick angling licence IS required for freshwater/inland species such as brook trout and Atlantic salmon. See each species' own guide for full current bag limits, seasons, and size limits — DFO issues variation orders that can change dates and limits with little notice.

sections.heading: Striped Bass
sections.body_md:
**Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: The Cocagne River mouth and marina breakwater; the Shediac River and Scoudouc River mouths into Shediac Bay; Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf on a moving tide. Bass here are believed to be transient fish out of the Miramichi system spreading along the Gulf coast, not a local spawning population.

**Key pattern**: Follow the current and the baitfish (smelt, gaspereau, small eels are key forage). Fish get more spread out — and often more catchable in the surf/open coast — later in the season as they disperse from the Miramichi. Low light (dawn, dusk, after dark within legal hours) and a bit of wave action/current disturbance both tend to outfish dead-calm, crowded daytime conditions.

**Best lures & retrieves**: bucktail jig (1/2-1 oz) cast across current and swum near bottom; soft plastic swimbait/jerk shad cast down-and-across and swung on a falling tide; topwater plug worked low-light only; marabou jig with a slow pulsing lift-and-drop. **Best bait**: a chunk of cut mackerel fished on the bottom on a single barbless hook.

**Gear fit**: MH rod, 20 lb braid / 20 lb fluoro leader.

sources.label: Outdoor Canada, New Brunswick's Striped Bass Bonanza

sections.heading: Atlantic Mackerel
sections.body_md:
**Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf is a well-known, easy mackerel spot right off the dock; the Cocagne breakwater and any wharf with tidal current in Shediac Bay are also worth checking. Mackerel push close to shore mainly from August into the fall.

**Key pattern**: They travel in schools — watch for diving gulls/terns and jumping baitfish (silversides). Best around high tidal current.

**Best lures**: sabiki/feather rig jigged slowly; small shiny casting spoon retrieved fast and steady; small metal jig worked at different depths.

**Gear fit**: ML rod, 20 lb braid / 12 lb mono.

sections.heading: Winter Flounder
sections.body_md:
**Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Sandy/muddy estuary bottom — the Cocagne River mouth and Shediac Bay's shallower stretches near the Shediac and Scoudouc river mouths are classic flounder water.

**Key pattern**: Bottom-dwelling; fish directly on bottom with light, subtle presentations. **Rig**: hi-lo bottom rig tipped with clam strips, squid strips, sandworms, or scented soft plastics, cast out and retrieved slowly with frequent multi-second pauses — bites are subtle nibbles, not hard strikes.

sources.label: Salt Water Sportsman, Winter Flounder Fishing Tips

sections.heading: Rainbow Smelt
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Estuary shallows and river mouths, e.g. the Cocagne and Shediac River mouths — mainly a spring spawning-run fish, but present through the season near structure in summer. **Method**: locate a school and target its edge with a tiny bucktail jighead or small streamer fly, retrieved steadily toward you — takes usually happen as the lure leaves the school.

sections.heading: Gaspereau (Alewife)
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: River mouths and lower estuary stretches of the Cocagne and Shediac Rivers — they run upriver a few weeks after the smelt run (typically May), with stragglers findable near estuary mouths into summer. Strong fighters for their size and prone to jumping when hooked. **Method**: small white streamer fly (size 8-12) or similarly small light jighead, swung with a swift consistent pace. Not good table fare — plan to release.

sections.heading: White Perch
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Estuaries and any barrier-beach ponds in the area — reported as present around Cap-Lumière and Cocagne on this same stretch of coast. Much less selective than most species here — a consistent, high-action producer once located. **Method**: small spinner retrieved at a steady moderate pace, or a float/bobber rig with bait.

sources.label: fishingreminder.com, New Brunswick fishing spots overview

sections.heading: American Eel
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Estuaries throughout the area hold eel populations — the Cocagne and Shediac River systems both qualify. Eels hunt almost entirely by smell, not sight — one of the few species here where lures/flies are largely ineffective. **Method**: cut fish, worms, or other scented bait fished directly on the bottom, and wait.

sections.heading: Cunner (Bergall)
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Around docks, wharves, and piers — Shediac Harbour is specifically noted as good cunner water. Aggressive, opportunistic, and very good at stealing bait — a reliably easy, fun species. **Method**: drop a small bait rig straight down beside pilings/rocks; no special retrieve needed.

sections.heading: Tomcod & Sculpin
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: Deeper estuary water in the Cocagne and Shediac systems — both are commonly caught incidentally while targeting winter flounder. Cocagne Cove specifically lists 'Grubby sculpin' among its notable catches. Small fish — treat as bonus catches on flounder gear rather than dedicated targets.

sections.heading: Brook Trout / Sea-Run Brook Trout (freshwater bonus option)
sections.body_md: **Where near Cocagne/Shediac**: The Cocagne River and Shediac River both hold brook trout, including sea-run fish in their tidal/estuary reaches. Requires a valid NB angling licence — an inland-water fishery, separate from the tidal saltwater species above. Sea-run fish are best targeted late spring/early summer as they push into estuaries to feed; by mid-summer the push has typically passed.

spots.name: Cocagne Cape Marina & breakwater
spots.description: The classic local spot at the mouth of the Cocagne River; striped bass have been fished off the breakwater, plus general estuary species.

spots.name: Cocagne River mouth / Cocagne Cove
spots.description: Estuary water noted for striped bass, mackerel, and sculpin.

spots.name: Pointe-du-Chêne Wharf
spots.description: Iconic, easy-access wharf fishing on Shediac Bay; visiting anglers regularly report catching mackerel right off the dock. Small daily parking fee.

spots.name: Parlee Beach Provincial Park
spots.description: Open Shediac Bay beach frontage next to Pointe-du-Chêne; good surf/beach casting water and some of the warmest ocean water north of the Carolinas.

spots.name: Shediac River mouth / Shediac Bridge
spots.description: River-mouth current into Shediac Bay; holds striped bass and brook trout.

spots.name: Shediac Harbour
spots.description: Good wharf fishing for striped bass, mackerel, and cunner.

spots.name: Miramichi system (worth the drive)
spots.description: Roughly 1.5 hours north; the source river system for most Gulf-coast striped bass and New Brunswick's premier Atlantic salmon water.
